name: spillway
description: Spillway — the control plane where AI spend is governed, not just observed.
_comment_overrides: Transitive security floors. Never put the ADVISORY FLOOR in the selector: 'fast-uri@>=3.0.0 <3.1.4' stopped matching the moment the lockfile reached 3.1.4, so when the floor later moved to 3.1.5 the override went inert and Ring 0 went red with 'security_update_not_possible' — the override was capping the fix it existed to deliver. Put the floor in the VALUE. A bound at a MAJOR BOUNDARY ('nanoid@>=3.0.0 <4.0.0') is a different thing and is fine: it never goes inert for its own line, and it is required whenever a package has several live major lines that must not be forced onto each other.
_comment_overrides_brace_expansion: CORRECTION 2026-08-16: this entry used to be annotated 'brace-expansion keeps a >=4.0.0 selector because 1.x/2.x are not vulnerable'. That is no longer true — advisories now cover <1.1.18 and >=2.0.0 <2.1.4, and the tree carried 1.1.15 and 2.1.1. The other half of that note still holds: forcing 5.x onto the legacy lines breaks minimatch. So each major line gets its own floor on its own line rather than one selector.
_comment_overrides_esbuild: esbuild is deliberately NOT overridden. The vulnerable copies (0.18.20, 0.19.12) come from drizzle-kit, the migration tool; vite and tsx already carry 0.25.12/0.28.1 and are unaffected. Forcing drizzle-kit onto 0.25+ to clear a MODERATE dev-only advisory risks breaking migrations, which is a far worse outcome than the advisory. Revisit if it is ever reachable from the production tree or the severity rises.

scripts.gate: pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test && pnpm test:web && pnpm test:integration && pnpm migration-lint && pnpm build
scripts.build:packages: pnpm -F @spillway/shared build && pnpm -F @spillway/pricing build && pnpm -F @spillway/certifier build
scripts.build: pnpm build:packages && pnpm -F web build && tsc -p apps/server/tsconfig.build.json

_comment_undici: tools/stress imports MockAgent from undici and hands it to the server as the data-plane dispatcher. The dispatcher contract is NOT stable across undici majors: a v8 MockAgent handed to v7's fetch never answers — no error, the request just hangs until UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT at 300s. That is exactly what happened when @testcontainers/postgresql 10->12 (2026-08-09) swapped the hoisted undici the root had been borrowing from 5.29.0 to 8.9.0; nightly stress went red for eight days with a bare 'fetch failed'. This entry exists so root stops borrowing: keep the major EQUAL to apps/server's undici, and move both together or not at all.
